Trail Physics · Unit 3: Forces & Cornering · Module 8

Friction, Slopes and Springs

Newton’s laws at work: the normal force, static and kinetic friction, inclined planes, Hooke’s law and how materials deform.

Lesson coming

The question

Why does a tire grip, and why does it suddenly let go?

The physics

  • Normal force
  • Gravity on an incline
  • Static and kinetic friction
  • Coefficient of friction
  • Hooke’s law
  • Stress and strain

The math

  • F_f ≤ μ_s N (static), F_f = μ_k N (kinetic)
  • F_s = −kx
  • on a slope: N = mg cos θ, along the slope: mg sin θ

About the model: Friction coefficients in these labs are illustrative, not measured tire data.

Learning objectives

  • Find the normal force, on flat ground and on a slope
  • Use the friction model F_f = μN for static and kinetic friction
  • Split gravity into parts along and across a slope
  • Use Hooke’s law for a spring
  • Describe elastic deformation, stress and strain

Helps to know first: Newton’s Laws of Motion.

The mountain biking connection

Traction, braking, climbing and suspension are all applications of Newton’s laws: friction between rubber and dirt, gravity pulling along a slope, and springs pushing back when they compress.
